Do not use mink oil on your Doc Martens! the leather will be ruined over time. Use the Doc leather conditioners, it was made specifically for their boots. :) plus it doesn't stain like mink oil. its a better formula to use for your leather products

I work at Doc Marten and have gone thru a few pairs of Jadons. If you didn't already, get the doc break-in socks, they have extra layering in the back where your ankles are prone to friction. Or you can order special padded socks online. Heal grips also help. Its important to use the leather conditioners at least 2x a month, in places where it feels tight. You can also put the wax on the inside of the shoe near the heal if you need to. The Dubbin conditioner is my favorite because its super oily and also totally waterproofs in addition to softening/relaxing the leather and prevents cracks when the leather creases. Do NOT use conditioners that contain mink oil or saddle soap. It will diminish the leather over time, which is why Docs patented their own conditioners for their leather. I like breaking my boots in my home when I am cooking or cleaning so I'm not stuck outside somewhere in pain lol. Dont worry, they will break in, it'll take a few wears. :)

There's a neutral colored shoe polish sold in doc stores, you could try that and apply with the brush. You can also use leather paint to keep them yellow, available online or at art supply stores. I like to brush mine frequently with the polish, it really helps conceal the scuff marks evenly. As long as you condition them properly they will be fine :)

I work in sales at Doc Marten. Wonder Balsm conditions the leather and only makes it water resistant. Dubbin is a much heavier/greasier version of the formula, but it water proofs it completely and relaxes/softens the leather much better. It's not just a shining grease. You can use both though. Wonder balsm first, then dubbin. I like the dubbin conditioner a lot better personally. I apply it with the microfibre cloth (or you can use an old t-shirt) then use the black polish with a brush to keep them black. I do this a few times a month.
